questions.stem: A teenager who is very active in sports needs more energy from their diet compared to an elderly person with a sedentary lifestyle. Which nutrient group should provide most of the extra energy?

options.text: Vitamins and minerals
Water
Carbohydrates, as they are the body's main energy source
Fibre

questions.explanation: Carbohydrates are the body's primary and preferred energy source, especially during physical activity. Active teenagers need more carbohydrate-rich foods (pasta, rice, bread, potatoes) to fuel their muscles during exercise. While lipids also provide energy (more per gram), carbohydrates are more quickly available.

questions.stem: A person consistently eats more calories than their body uses. What is the most likely long-term health consequence?

options.text: Anaemia
Obesity, increasing the risk of type 2 diabetes, cardiovascular disease, and certain cancers
Scurvy
Marasmus

questions.explanation: When energy intake exceeds energy expenditure, the excess is stored as fat, leading to weight gain and eventually obesity. Obesity is a major risk factor for type 2 diabetes (insulin resistance), cardiovascular disease (high blood pressure, coronary heart disease), some cancers, and joint problems.

questions.stem: A pregnant woman is advised to increase her intake of folic acid (vitamin B9). Why is this particularly important?

options.text: Folic acid provides energy for the growing baby
Folic acid helps prevent neural tube defects (such as spina bifida) in the developing baby
Folic acid prevents the mother from gaining too much weight
Folic acid is needed for the mother's bone strength

questions.explanation: Folic acid is essential for proper neural tube development in the early stages of pregnancy. A deficiency increases the risk of neural tube defects such as spina bifida, where the spinal cord does not develop properly. This is why folic acid supplements are recommended before conception and during early pregnancy.

questions.stem: Dietary fibre (roughage) cannot be digested by humans. Why is it still an important part of a balanced diet?

options.text: Fibre provides essential amino acids
Fibre adds bulk to food, stimulating peristalsis and preventing constipation
Fibre is absorbed in the stomach and provides vitamins
Fibre replaces the need for water in the diet

questions.explanation: Although fibre cannot be digested, it provides bulk to the contents of the intestine. This stimulates peristalsis (the muscular contractions that push food through the gut), helping food move through the digestive system efficiently and preventing constipation. A high-fibre diet is also linked to reduced risk of bowel cancer.

questions.stem: A vegan diet excludes all animal products. Which nutrient might a vegan need to supplement, and why?

options.text: Carbohydrates, because they are only found in animal products
Vitamin B12, because it is primarily found in animal products and is needed for nerve function and red blood cell production
Fibre, because plants do not contain fibre
Water, because only animal products contain water

questions.explanation: Vitamin B12 is naturally found almost exclusively in animal products (meat, dairy, eggs). It is essential for nerve function, red blood cell formation, and DNA synthesis. Vegans need to obtain B12 from fortified foods or supplements to prevent deficiency, which can cause anaemia and neurological problems.
